q: What is the primary purpose of the research conducted by Candice Grace C. Maque?
a: The research aims to determine the influence of the Population Commission of the Philippines' Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign on the knowledge, attitude, and practices regarding HIV/AIDS among students at Pooc National High School – Senior High School Department.

q: What were the main findings regarding the effectiveness of the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign?
a: The Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign significantly influenced the knowledge, attitude, and practices of students exposed to the campaign compared to those in the control group. Additionally, students showed significant differences in these areas when comparing their pre-exposure scores to their post-exposure scores.

q: What research design and method did the researcher use to investigate HIV/AIDS awareness?
a: The researcher employed a quasi-experimental pre-test post-test two-group design. Data were collected from 179 randomly sampled students using self-administered questionnaires before and after a two-hour lecture PowerPoint presentation.

q: What are the key conclusions regarding the use of structured educational campaigns for youth health?
a: The Heart to H.E.A.R.T. Talk campaign showed an influence on the knowledge, attitude, and practices on HIV/AIDS of the students exposed to the campaign compared to those who were not.

q: Which specific variables were measured to assess the impact of the intervention?
a: The dependent variables measured were the students' knowledge, attitudes, and practices concerning HIV/AIDS. The independent variable was the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign implemented via a two-hour lecture.

q: What statistical tests were used to analyze the data collected from the students?
a: Data analysis included descriptive analysis, Fisher’s t-test, Chi-square, and McNemar’s test.

q: How was the intervention delivered to the participants?
a: The intervention was delivered as a two-hour lecture supported by a PowerPoint presentation.

q: How does the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign function as an educational intervention?
a: The campaign functions as an intervention through a two-hour lecture PowerPoint presentation. It aims to influence knowledge, attitude, and practices regarding HIV/AIDS.

q: What specific metrics showed significant differences between the exposed group and the control group in the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign?
a: The Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign showed significant differences in knowledge scores, attitudes, and practices. These differences were observed when comparing those exposed to the campaign against those in the control group.

q: How did the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign affect the knowledge scores of the participants?
a: The campaign resulted in a significant difference in knowledge scores for those exposed to it. This difference was evident when comparing participants before and after their exposure to the campaign.

q: Did the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign influence the practices of the individuals involved?
a: Yes, there was a significant difference in the practices of those exposed to the campaign. This difference was noted both when compared to a control group and when comparing pre-exposure to post-exposure states.

q: How did the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign compare to the control group regarding participant knowledge?
a: There was a significant difference in knowledge scores between those exposed to the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign and those in the control group. This comparison highlights the impact of the campaign on knowledge levels.

q: In what areas did the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign show significant differences compared to the control group?
a: The campaign showed significant differences in knowledge scores, attitudes, and practices. These areas were measured against the control group that was not exposed to the campaign.

q: How did the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign affect participant practices in relation to the control group?
a: There was a significant difference in the practices of those exposed to the campaign compared to those in the control group. This indicates that the campaign influenced participant practices.

q: What was the significance of the pre- and post-exposure comparison for participant practices in the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign?
a: There was a significant difference in the practices of participants before and after their exposure to the campaign. This shows that the intervention led to changes in practices.

q: Did the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign lead to significant changes in participant attitudes over time?
a: Yes, there was a significant difference in the attitudes of those exposed to the campaign before and after exposure. This indicates a temporal change in attitude due to the campaign.

q: What was the relationship between campaign exposure and knowledge scores in the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign?
a: Exposure to the campaign resulted in a significant difference in knowledge scores. This was observed both when comparing exposed individuals to a control group and when comparing participants before and after exposure.

q: What were the significant findings regarding attitudes in the Heart to H.E.A.R.T. campaign?
a: Significant differences were found in the attitudes of those exposed to the campaign compared to the control group. Additionally, significant differences were found in attitudes before and after exposure to the campaign.

q: What was the primary purpose of the research conducted by Mejia Jr. C. Felipe?
a: The research aimed to determine how Facebook use influenced the voting behavior of millennials in Taguig City, Philippines, during the 2019 mid-term senatorial election. It specifically examined if social media functions as a tool for political communication that impacts the decision-making processes of young voters.

q: What were the main findings regarding the functions of social media for millennials?
a: Millennials agreed that social media always serves to increase voting right awareness, create social consciousness, act as a campaign platform, and promote public engagement. The platform also helps them understand voting power, raise voices against political misdeeds, and learn about the activities and commitments of candidates.

q: How did Facebook influence the actual voting choices and views of the millennials studied?
a: Respondents reported being influenced only "sometime" by Facebook regarding their election views and choice of political leaders. While social media is a constant presence, the majority of participants claimed to rely "always" on their own personal decision-making when casting votes.

q: Why might millennials not read extensive amounts of campaign information on Facebook?
a: Voters may not read much information because they often maintain consistent opinions of candidates or political parties over time. This suggests that experienced voters are not easily swayed by campaign rhetoric.

q: Who is the primary demographic focus of this research?
a: The research focuses on millennials living in Taguig City, Philippines. Specifically, it looked at those within the researcher's Facebook network during the 2019 mid-term senatorial election.

q: What are the limitations regarding the influence of external sources on the respondents?
a: Respondents reported that they only "sometimes" relied on the influence of social media, other media, or interpersonal sources like family and friends. They instead relied "always" on their own personal decision-making.

q: What is the central problem addressed in the research regarding the relationship between schools and industry?
a: The research addresses how effective communication and the management of social exchanges can facilitate the creation of a functional linkage between an academic institution and an industry partner. Specifically, it looks at establishing a Contact Center Services program for the BPO industry.

q: What were the main findings regarding the success of the Contact Center Services program?
a: The establishment of the program was successful due to an optimal mix of exchange goals, resources, rules, and communication. The findings show that exchange goals were primarily cooperative and the partnership was driven by 'Group Gain'.

q: What specific communication roles were identified as being used during the partnership?
a: The researcher utilized various roles including Linker/Networker, facilitator, negotiator, and catalyst. The Linker/Networker role was notably used to bring together individuals with different types of knowledge and expertise.

q: How does the researcher describe the role of communication within social exchanges?
a: Communication is identified as an enabling variable during social exchanges. A successful linkage agent must assess exchange variables to determine which communication role is most appropriate to assume.

q: What resources were utilized to facilitate the partnership between the school and the BPO company?
a: The parties utilized accessible and 'cheap' resources, specifically in the form of services and information. Additionally, the researcher used 'love' or friendship to facilitate smoother interactions and transactions.

q: What role did the researcher play in the establishment of the program?
a: The researcher acted as a negotiator-liaison between the public high school and the partner BPO company. This role involved navigating complex exchanges among various stakeholders.

q: What importance does understanding power dynamics hold for a linkage agent?
a: Navigating partnerships requires understanding unique power dynamics, including the extent of stakeholder influence over outcomes and their relative positions of support. A linkage agent must also know when to shift roles or withdraw to avoid endangering the partnership.

q: What is the implication of having a long history of collaborative relationships between parties?
a: A long history of collaborative and productive relationships can serve as a buffer for partnerships. This history can help sustain a partnership even during periods when the involved parties are dissatisfied with specific outcomes.

q: What is the specific context and location of the research?
a: The research is situated within the implementation of the K-12 curriculum in a public high school in San Pedro, Laguna, Philippines. It focuses on a training-to-employment program for the Business Process Outsourcing industry.

q: What communication roles can a negotiator-liaison assume to manage a partnership?
a: A negotiator-liaison can assume the roles of linker/networker, facilitator, negotiator, or catalyst. The choice of role depends on an assessment of exchange goals, rules, and resources.

q: What is the central purpose of the research regarding the #HealthXPH network?
a: The research examines how sixty-two participants of the #HealthXPH network use Twitter for healthcare practice, learning, and collaboration. It specifically investigates user motivations and evaluates whether the platform meets the needs of these users.

q: What are the main findings regarding user motivations in the #HealthXPH network?
a: Users are primarily driven by information-seeking motivations. However, results indicate that Twitter does not fully satisfy these specific information-seeking motivations for the participants.

q: How do media attributes like usability and interactivity relate to user gratifications?
a: Usability and interactivity have a significant relationship with both the information-seeking gratifications sought and those obtained. These attributes are key to how users engage with the platform.

q: How do usage patterns influence the gratifications obtained by #HealthXPH members?
a: The amount of time spent on Twitter is significantly related to interpersonal utility obtained. Additionally, the length of time a person has been a Twitter user relates to information-seeking gratifications obtained.

q: How does the #HealthXPH network facilitate learning and collaboration on Twitter?
a: Participants use the platform to crowdsource experience, expertise, and ideas. This is primarily achieved through moderated online discussions called tweet chats that utilize the hashtag feature.

q: What are the primary uses of the collaborative processes found within the network?

q: What are the main findings regarding the listenership of Pandan Community Radio's nutritional programs?

q: How did the researcher evaluate the satisfaction of audience needs?

The findings showed that all programs except "Lingkod Bayan sa Sabado Tugstugan" and "Senior Citizen’s Hour" gratified these five basic needs.

q: What is the primary purpose of the research conducted by Maria Victoria A. Cariño?
a: The research aims to determine the association between interpersonal communication elements, participant profiles, and uncertainty reduction among women in the Pabasa sa Nutrisyon program. This program is an information-sharing activity designed to educate mothers on meal selection and preparation to prevent malnutrition.

q: Which interpersonal communication elements are most closely linked to uncertainty reduction?
a: Context and channel were found to be highly associated with uncertainty reduction. Specifically, the physical dimension of the learning environment and the interpersonal channel involving direct contact with the Barangay Nutrition Scholar (BNS) and peers are crucial.

q: What methodology was used to analyze the data from the 222 women participating in the program?
a: The study employed a quantitative approach using descriptive statistics. Data analysis included the use of frequency counts, percentages, and Spearman’s rho correlation coefficient.

q: Which participant profiles are associated with higher levels of uncertainty reduction?
a: Younger participants, those with a college-level education, and mothers with healthy children registered higher degrees of uncertainty reduction. These demographic characteristics were found to be significant in the study.

q: Which uncertainty reduction strategy proved to be the most effective for the participants?
a: The interactive strategy, which involves asking the source directly for information, was identified as the most effective method. This strategy is considered the most potent tool for participants to gain clarity.

q: How does the social context of the Pabasa sa Nutrisyon influence the learning process?
a: Mothers prefer a learning environment where they can learn alongside and from their fellow mothers and the Barangay Nutrition Scholar (BNS). This social dimension is a key component of the context that aids in reducing uncertainty.

q: What role does the Barangay Nutrition Scholar (BNS) play in the communication process?
a: The BNS serves as the Pabasa leader and a primary source of information. Direct contact with the BNS, combined with the presence of other participants, aids in the reduction of uncertainty.

q: What demographic factors related to age and status influence how uncertainty is reduced?
a: Age characteristics and the type of participant were seen to reduce uncertainty. Specifically, young mothers with healthy kids who reached college registered a higher uncertainty reduction compared to other participants.

q: How do interpersonal communication channels facilitate information sharing in this context?
a: Uncertainty reduction is aided by the interpersonal channel, which includes personal presence and direct contact with the Barangay Nutrition Scholar and other participants. This is further supplemented by the use of printed materials.

q: What communication strategies are used by participants to gather information?
a: Participants use interactive, active, and passive strategies to manage uncertainty. The interactive strategy, which involves direct questioning of the source, was found to be the most effective method for gaining clarity.

q: Which constructive journalistic frames are most prevalent in reports on European migration?
a: The most present frames are identified in Chapter 4. These findings highlight the most common approaches used in constructive news.

q: What were the main findings regarding the relationship between gratification sought and gratification obtained?

q: How can the ONON program bridge the gap between seeking information and obtaining actionable medical guidance?

q: Who is the target demographic for this research?

q: What theoretical framework guided the analysis of radio listening gratification?

q: What specific health-related topics showed the largest gap between listener expectations and actual experiences?
a: Listeners experienced gaps regarding the presentation of symptoms and the prevention of certain diseases caused by poor nutrition. There was also a gap regarding the presence of health experts to provide advice on disease prevention.

q: What is the implication of the presence of health experts in the radio program?
a: The presence of health experts seems to communicate the importance of immediate feedback should listeners decide to call the radio station for advice or response to questions needing some answers.

q: How does the ONON radio program address the prevention of diseases related to nutrition?
a: The program includes the presence of health experts to advise on how to prevent diseases. It also features the presentation of symptoms and the prevention of certain diseases that could be due to poor nutrition.

q: What role does medical guidance play in the motivations of the mothers surveyed?

q: What is the central purpose of the research conducted by Marjorie Naguimbing-Manlulu?
a: The research aims to describe the narratives embedded in 31 climate change news stories from three major Philippine newspapers, identify the narrative norms used by Filipino journalists, and determine their subject positions.

q: What are the four primary narratives identified in the Philippine print news media regarding climate change?
a: The four narratives are international cooperation, government 'wars' against climate change, climate justice, and science as an answer to climate change.

q: What methodological approach was used to analyze the climate change news stories?
a: The study utilized a dual-methodological approach combining Arnold's (2015) integrated model of cultural narrative analysis with narratological analysis.

q: How did the subject position of Filipino journalists manifest in the analyzed news stories?
a: Journalists emerged as loyal facilitators of politicians, portraying those politicians in a positive light as advocates for climate action.

q: What specific narrative norms did Filipino journalists employ when writing about climate change?
a: Journalists used six techniques: announcements, quotations/reports, narration, re-narration, metaphor, and summary.

q: How did journalists handle characterization while attempting to maintain professional objectivity?
a: Journalists used figural characterization to portray villains, victims, and heroes through other characters, while limiting narratorial characterization to verifiable descriptions.

q: What significant deficiency was found in the representation of voices within the news stories?
a: There was a lack of character diversity, meaning mainstream news media failed to provide a platform for diverse views, especially those of the marginalized.

q: What does the research recommend for the future of journalistic practice in the Philippines?
a: The research recommends practicing the principles of development journalism within mainstream news organizations to provide a platform for diverse voices.

q: How did the subject position of journalists influence the construction of climate change narratives?
a: Journalists acted as loyal facilitators of politicians, shaping narratives that portrayed political advocates for climate action in a positive light.

q: What role does development journalism play in the recommendations of this research?
a: The study suggests that adopting development journalism principles could help media organizations fulfill their duty to serve as platforms for diverse voices.

q: How is the relationship between climate action and national development framed in the news stories?
a: The research identified a sub-narrative involving an internal struggle between pursuing climate action and maintaining national development.

q: In what way is environmental degradation emphasized through the use of thematic space?
a: Journalists specifically utilized thematic space within their narratives to emphasize the issue of environmental degradation.

q: What is the proposed solution for news media to better address the complex problem of climate change?
a: News media can fulfill its duty by becoming a platform for diverse voices. This can be achieved through the formation of organizations that advocate for the tenets of development journalism.

q: How can news media fulfill its duty regarding the complex problem of climate change?
a: News media can fulfill this duty by acting as a platform for diverse voices. This is linked to the advocacy of development journalism tenets.

q: What role do organizations advocating development journalism play in addressing climate change?
a: These organizations advocate for tenets that allow news media to become a platform for diverse voices. This process is intended to help solve the complex problem of climate change.

q: What is the central purpose of Geff B. Sagala's research regarding Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) in Saudi Arabia?
a: The research study determined the relationship of communication strategies with the level of awareness and level of preparedness, and how these variables affected cognitive dissonance. It assessed the level of awareness on Saudi Vision 2030 and level of preparedness for eventual repatriation among seven hundred eight seven OFWs living and working in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

q: What are the main findings regarding the awareness levels of OFWs concerning Saudi Vision 2030?
a: Awareness of Saudi Vision 2030 is primarily achieved through social media, billboards, and digital advertisements. Information is also spread through word of mouth within the OFW community, government websites, and traditional media like TV and newspapers.

q: What is the level of preparedness among the surveyed Overseas Filipino Workers for their eventual repatriation?
a: Majority of OFWs are preparing for eventual repatriation.

q: What theoretical framework is used to examine the relationship between communication strategies and worker readiness?
a: The research is premised on Festinger’s Cognitive Dissonance theory. This framework is used to examine how communication strategies correlate with awareness and preparedness, with cognitive dissonance acting as a mediating variable.

q: What specific communication channels were identified as contributing to awareness among OFWs?
a: Awareness is driven by social media, billboards, digital advertisements, government websites, and traditional media like television and newspapers. Additionally, word of mouth within the OFW community plays a significant role in spreading information.

q: Which media channels were most effective in spreading awareness of Saudi Vision 2030 among OFWs?
a: Awareness was primarily achieved through social media, billboards, and digital advertisements. Traditional media outlets like television and newspapers, along with government websites, also contributed to spreading information.

q: What is the central problem investigated in the research regarding the residents of Lobo, Batangas?
a: The research investigates how specific communication factors serve to define and shape the perceptions held by the residents of Lobo, Batangas, regarding the ecotourism industry. It specifically addresses the gaps between the field of ecotourism and the field of communication.

q: What are the main findings regarding how residents of Lobo, Batangas acquire information about ecotourism?
a: The majority of respondents acquire ecotourism information through television and tourism organizations or associations. These residents are most frequently exposed to messages that revolve around the nature-based tenet of ecotourism.

q: What is the level of ego-involvement among the residents of Lobo, Batangas, toward ecotourism?
a: The residents demonstrate a high level of ego-involvement, with the majority considering the ecotourism concept and industry to be highly important in their lives. This high level of involvement significantly influences how they process information and form opinions.

q: What is the current perception of the ecotourism industry among the residents of Lobo, Batangas?
a: The findings indicate that the residents mostly perceive ecotourism positively. This perception is shaped by communication factors that act as carriers of meaning.

q: What theoretical framework guided the investigation into resident perceptions?
a: The investigation was guided by the Social Judgement Theory (SJT).

q: What are the key recommendations for the Local Government Unit (LGU) of Lobo, Batangas?
a: The LGU is recommended to coordinate with interpersonal sources and maximize the use of mediated sources to expand communication efforts. This would allow for more effective management of the information flow to the community.

q: What is the primary conclusion regarding the role of communication in ecotourism?
a: Communication factors define perceptions on ecotourism by being carriers of meanings that serve as the basis of how people perceive and act towards the industry.

q: Who would benefit from the recommendations provided in the research?
a: The Local Government Unit (LGU) of Lobo, Batangas, would benefit from the recommendations to expand their communication efforts. Future researchers could also benefit from the suggestion to use random sampling methods.

q: What mediated sources do residents of Lobo, Batangas, use to learn about ecotourism?
a: Television is identified as one of the primary mediated sources for ecotourism information. The study also notes that communication factors act as carriers of meanings that shape resident perceptions.

q: How do communication factors influence the way residents of Lobo, Batangas, act toward ecotourism?
a: Communication factors define perceptions on ecotourism by acting as carriers of meanings that serve as the basis for how residents perceive and act towards the industry.

q: What specific theme is most common in the ecotourism messages received by residents?
a: The messages encountered by residents most frequently revolve around the nature-based tenet of ecotourism. This content helps define the residents' understanding of the industry.

q: How does the level of ego-involvement relate to the ecotourism industry in Lobo, Batangas?
a: Most residents consider the ecotourism industry to be highly important in their lives. This high level of ego-involvement influences how they process information related to the industry.

q: What research design and theoretical framework were used to investigate KMC awareness?

q: What is the central purpose of the research conducted by Ralson M. Hernandez?
a: The research aims to understand how Filipinos living with HIV/AIDS perceive themselves and build relationships through interpersonal communication. It specifically seeks to identify self-concept themes, describe interaction experiences, and identify types of relationships maintained by these individuals.

q: What are the different forms of communication identified in the research?
a: Communication forms include verbal and face-to-face interaction in dyadic or small group settings, non-verbal cues like hugging or smiling, public communication, and computer-mediated communication (CMC) such as social media and group chats.

q: How are the relationships of Filipinos living with HIV/AIDS categorized?
a: Relationships are classified into four types: The First Line, The Small Circle, The Online Friends, and The Others. These are further grouped into Close-Open, where individuals open up to close contacts, and Consensus Reality, where individuals discuss their condition with others experiencing the same case.

q: What are the limitations regarding the participant demographic in this research?

q: What are the implications for future health communication research in the Philippines?

q: What is the primary purpose of the research conducted by Maria Loida D. Irabagon?
a: The research aims to determine the knowledge levels of 120 upland and lowland rice farmers in Nueva Ecija, Philippines, regarding climate change. It specifically seeks to validate the Knowledge Gap Theory by examining the relationship between socio-economic status and knowledge levels.

q: What are the main findings regarding the climate change knowledge of rice farmers in Nueva Ecija?
a: Upland and lowland farmers are knowledgeable about the causes, effects, impacts, and government programs related to climate change. However, they possess only slight knowledge regarding technical aspects and are often unfamiliar with recommended adaptation technologies.

q: What specific knowledge gap was identified among the farmer respondents?
a: A significant gap exists in technical knowledge concerning climate change. Additionally, many farmers lack familiarity with recommended adaptation technologies because these technologies have not been introduced to them.

q: How do local government units in Nueva Ecija contribute to climate change education?
a: LGUs in Carranglan, Palayan City, and San Isidro actively disseminate knowledge and adaptation technologies through seminars, Farmers Field School, and Lakbay-Aral. In contrast, Guimba had the fewest agricultural extension activities regarding climate change adaptation.

q: Which academic and research institutions assist in educating farmers on climate change?
a: Araullo University, Central Luzon State University, and the Central Luzon Agriculture and Aquatic Resources Research and Development Consortium contribute to farmer education through various communication activities.

q: What are the key recommendations for local government units to address information gaps?
a: Local government units are encouraged to strengthen their extension services and foster partnerships to improve the dissemination of information and technologies. The continuous implementation of the Farmers Field School is specifically recommended.

q: Who is the primary audience that benefits from the findings of this research?
a: The findings are relevant to local government units for policy making and researchers interested in the social and communication factors of knowledge gaps. It also serves those involved in agricultural extension and climate change adaptation.

q: What is the significance of the Knowledge Gap Theory in this research context?
a: The Knowledge Gap Theory is used to hypothesize that socio-economic status influences the level of knowledge a person possesses. The study tests this theory by looking at the relationship between the socio-economic status of farmers and their understanding of climate change.

q: What agricultural extension methods are used to promote climate change adaptation?
a: Local government units utilize seminars, Farmers Field School, and Lakbay-Aral to disseminate adaptation technologies. These activities are intended to help farmers manage the impacts of climate change on their crops.

q: What role do academic institutions play in communicating climate change information?
a: Institutions such as Araullo University and Central Luzon State University conduct communication activities to educate farmers. These efforts help bridge the gap in climate change knowledge among the agricultural community.

q: How many rice farmers in Nueva Ecija participated in the research?
a: The research involved 120 respondents consisting of upland rice farmers and lowland rice farmers. These participants were located in Nueva Ecija, Philippines.

q: What specific theory does the research aim to validate?
a: The research aims to validate the Knowledge Gap Theory proposed by Tichenor, Donohue, and Olien. This validation involves examining the relationship between socio-economic status and climate change knowledge levels.

q: Which specific institutions provided communication activities to educate the farmers?
a: Araullo University, Central Luzon State University, and the Central Luzon Agriculture and Aquatic Resources Research and Development Consortium provided communication activities. These institutions helped educate the respondents regarding climate change.

q: What is the recommended focus for future researchers studying knowledge gaps?
a: Researchers should explore the effects of social and communication factors when studying knowledge gaps. This is especially important when testing knowledge that is global in nature or includes technological interventions.

q: What specific extension service should local government units strengthen?
a: Local government units are recommended to strengthen their extension services regarding climate change. This is part of the recommendations to address information dissemination at the local level.

q: What agricultural program is recommended for continuous implementation?
a: The continuous implementation of the Farmers Field School is recommended. This recommendation is intended to support climate change education and information dissemination.

q: What is the central purpose of the research conducted by Rosario?
a: The research aims to understand and describe how Philippine-based companies communicate Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives to ensure beneficiary mobilization for youth employability. It specifically seeks to identify effective communication strategies and recommend a model for implementing these initiatives.

q: What are the main findings regarding the effectiveness of communication strategies for beneficiary mobilization?
a: External communication strategies are more effective for mobilization than internal ones, with personal and digital communication identified as the most effective tools. The study also found that CSR initiatives are deeply embedded in the vision, mission, and core values of the participating companies.

q: What methodology was used to investigate the communication of CSR initiatives?
a: The researcher employed a Comparative Case Analysis methodology involving three Philippine-based companies. Data was gathered through Key Informant Interviews with managers and Program Officers, supplemented by a Document Analysis of websites, social media, blogs, and press releases.

q: How does the number of internship and scholarship slots relate to a company's financial status?
a: The study found that the number of available internship and scholarship slots may be proportional to a company's net income.

q: What are the theoretical frameworks used to analyze the communication process?
a: The study applies the Uses and Gratifications theory to understand how communication satisfies the needs of audiences and implementers. It also utilizes Mersham and Skinner's Theory of Communication to view communication as a successful two-way process when positive feedback is received through mobilization.

q: What are the practical implications of adopting the recommended mediated communication model?
a: Adopting this model ensures information reaches appropriate candidates, which reduces rework and saves time, energy, and resources. These saved operational expenses can then be redirected to provide more support for unemployed Filipino youth.

q: What gap in existing literature does this research address?
a: This research addresses the lack of studies regarding the implementation of CSR initiatives by Philippine-based companies that specifically target the employment needs of the country's youth.

q: Which communication strategies are utilized by the three Philippine-based companies for their CSR initiatives?
a: The three Philippine-based companies use a combination of Personal, Print, and Digital Communication. These strategies are categorized as both internal and external communication strategies.

q: How do external communication strategies compare to internal communication strategies regarding beneficiary mobilization?
a: External communication strategies allow for beneficiary mobilization more effectively than internal communication strategies. These external strategies are implemented by the three Philippine-based companies.

q: Which specific communication strategies are recommended to facilitate beneficiary mobilization?
a: The recommended communication strategies for facilitating beneficiary mobilization are Personal and Digital Communication. These are identified as the most effective among the strategies used by the three Philippine-based companies.

q: Through what entities do the three Philippine-based companies communicate their external CSR strategies?
a: External communication strategies are communicated through partner organizations such as foundations or schools. These organizations act as the medium for the companies' CSR initiatives.

q: What is the dual purpose of the mediated communication model used by the three Philippine-based companies?
a: The mediated communication model is implemented to achieve beneficiary mobilization. Additionally, this model serves to achieve partner mobilization as well.

q: How does the Uses and Gratifications theory explain beneficiary mobilization in these CSR initiatives?
a: Beneficiary mobilization is highly influenced by the gratification of the needs and motives of the target audiences and the implementors. This relationship is contextualized within the Uses and Gratifications theory.

q: What specific corporate needs are gratified by the targeted external communication strategies of the three Philippine-based companies?

q: What role do partner organizations play in the recommended external communication model?
a: Partner organizations act as both senders and receivers of encoded and decoded messages, such as calls for applications. They also serve to filter candidates before endorsing them to the companies.

q: What is the central problem addressed in Marlyn S. Tigo's research?
a: The research investigates the prevalence of domestic violence and the oppressive realities faced by Overseas Filipino Worker (OFW) domestic workers. These struggles present a significant challenge to the Philippine government and the workers themselves.

q: What are the main findings regarding the communication experiences of run-away domestic workers?
a: The findings identify four specific communication barriers: language barriers, semantic barriers, psychological attitude, and perceptions of reality. These communication struggles are deeply intertwined with the workers' overall vulnerability and oppressive working conditions.

q: What methodology was used to investigate the lived experiences of the participants?
a: The study employed a qualitative methodology using semi-structured interviews with four run-away domestic workers. The researcher utilized narrative analysis to examine how stories were told and to uncover different layers of meaning.

q: How does the research define the dual nature of domestic work?
a: Domestic work is described as potentially empowering through economic gain for families. Conversely, it can be oppressive due to poor working conditions, limited mobility, and vulnerability to abuse.

q: Why were the names of the participants changed in the research?
a: All names of the participants have been changed in this thesis to avoid repercussions with regard to domestic issue and illegal work.

q: What specific topics did participants reflect on during the semi-structured interviews?
a: Participants reflected on their motivations for working abroad, their domestic struggles, and the difficulties faced when communicating with employers and families. These reflections were captured through audio-recorded interviews.

q: What are the four specific communication barriers identified by the participants?
a: The identified barriers include language barriers, semantic barriers, psychological attitude, and perceptions of reality. These obstacles impact how domestic workers interact with others.

q: Why is communication considered particularly crucial for domestic workers?
a: Communication is essential to human life and is especially vital for domestic workers. This is because they must interact with foreign employers who may have limited communication skills.

q: What sequence of events did participants reveal regarding their employment struggles?
a: Participants revealed unfortunate situations starting from the moment they were hired through recruitment agencies or human traffickers. This process continued until they abandoned their jobs and ran away to seek legal assistance.

q: Where did run-away domestic workers go to seek legal assistance?
a: Run-away domestic workers sought legal assistance at the Philippine embassy. This occurred after they abandoned their jobs.

q: How does the research characterize the communication skills of foreign employers?
a: The research notes that domestic workers must deal with foreign employers who possess limited communication skills. This factor makes communication particularly crucial for the workers.

q: What method was used to capture the participants' reflections?
a: Semi-structured interviews were used to capture the participants' reflections. These interviews were audio-recorded and then transcribed.

q: What specific communication barrier relates to the meaning of words?
a: Semantic barriers are one of the four communication barriers identified by the participants. This is listed alongside language, psychological, and perceptual barriers.

q: What type of interview format was employed in the research?
a: The research employed semi-structured interviews. These allowed participants to reflect on their motivations, struggles, and communication difficulties.

q: What psychological factor acts as a communication barrier for the workers?
a: Psychological attitude is identified as one of the four communication barriers. It is categorized alongside semantic, language, and perception-based barriers.

q: How does the research describe the participants' motivation for working abroad?
a: The research uses semi-structured interviews to have participants reflect on their specific motivations for working abroad. This is part of the broader investigation into their domestic struggles.

q: What is the relationship between communication and human life in this context?
a: Communication is described as being crucial to human life. This importance is magnified for domestic workers who must navigate interactions with employers having limited communication skills.

q: What are the perceptions of reality in the context of communication barriers?
a: Perceptions of reality are identified as one of the four communication barriers experienced by the participants. This barrier contributes to the difficulties workers face when communicating.

q: What are the main findings regarding the relationship between educational materials and student behavior?
a: The study found a significant negative correlation between exposure to gender-biased educational communication materials and students' practices towards gender equality. This means that as exposure to gender-biased materials increases, students' practices towards gender equality decrease.

q: What theoretical framework did Krupskaya T. Valila use to examine these variables?
a: The research utilized the Exposure-Practice Framework, which is a hybrid model combining the Elaboration Likelihood Model and Mere Exposure Theory. This framework allowed for the examination of exposure to gender-sensitive materials as the independent variable and practices towards gender equality as the dependent variable.

q: What are the key conclusions regarding the role of teachers' instructional materials?
a: The exposure of students towards gender-biased educational communication materials was negatively correlated with the students’ practice towards gender equality. This means that as exposure to gender-biased educational communication materials increases, practices of students towards gender equality decreases.

q: Who is the primary population affected by the findings of this research?
a: The primary population affected by the findings is three hundred ninety-nine students from the Polytechnic University of the Philippines, Mabini Campus. These students were surveyed to determine their perception of the gender sensitivity of teachers’ educational communication materials and their practices towards gender equality.

q: How does exposure to biased educational materials affect the social behaviors of students regarding gender?
a: The exposure of students to gender-biased educational communication materials is negatively correlated with their practice towards gender equality. This means that as exposure to these materials increases, students' practices towards gender equality decrease.

q: What is the central problem addressed in the research regarding informal money lenders in Meycauayan City?
a: The research addresses the persistent demand for informal lenders despite their usurious practices. It explores the cognitive dissonance experienced by borrowers who rationalize their irrational behavior by viewing high interest rates as a trade-off for easy access to credit.

q: What are the main findings regarding the psychological state of borrowers in Barangay Pantoc?
a: The findings reveal that borrowers experience cognitive dissonance, which they resolve through forced compliance and rationalization. They justify their irrational behavior by perceiving usurious interest rates as a necessary trade-off for easy access to credit.

q: What role does financial literacy play in the engagement with informal lenders?
a: A lack of knowledge regarding fair and proper lending and borrowing practices is a significant factor in why respondents engage with informal lenders. Limited financial sophistication also makes cognitive dissonance less apparent to the respondents themselves.

q: How do borrowers react when informed that informal lenders are disadvantageous to their financial well-being?
a: Instead of changing their behavior, respondents engage in forced compliance. They resolve the resulting psychological discomfort by changing their perception of the action to justify the use of informal credit.

q: What are the primary recommendations for addressing the reliance on informal lenders?
a: The study recommends enhancing financial literacy programs to improve borrower sophistication. It also emphasizes the need to provide better access to affordable credit through the formal banking system.

q: Who is most affected by the findings of this research?
a: The findings are relevant to households in Barangay Pantoc, Meycauayan City, who rely on informal credit like '5-6' lending. It also matters to those involved in financial literacy and formal banking services.

q: What development-oriented interventions are suggested to improve financial well-being in the community?
a: The study recommends enhancing financial literacy programs to increase the sophistication of borrowers. Additionally, it suggests improving access to affordable credit through the formal banking system to provide an alternative to informal lenders.

q: What is the central problem addressed by the Eduk-Aksyon Program study?
a: The research addresses how to ensure behavioral changes, such as parents consistently prioritizing their children's education, are sustained even when government reinforcements like the Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) program are absent.

q: What are the main findings regarding the influence of the Eduk-Aksyon Program on parental behavior?
a: The Eduk-Aksyon Program led to sustained behavioral change in parents through 'communication through action,' such as the distribution of school supplies. This change was driven by a combination of external rewards and the parents' internal motivations.

q: What methodology was used to investigate parental perceptions in this research?
a: The researcher employed a qualitative methodology consisting of focused group discussions, interviews, and cross-case analyses. The participants were parents who continued to send their children to school without government financial assistance.

q: What specific factors within the Eduk-Aksyon Program did parents value most?
a: Parents highly valued the distribution of school supplies, the rewards and incentives systems, and the program's focus on holistic mental and spiritual development. These factors helped alleviate the financial burden of school overhead expenses.

q: What internal motivations drive parents to prioritize their children's education?
a: Parents are motivated by a personal and moral obligation to provide their children's right to education. They also hold a cognitive realization that education is the key to escaping the vicious cycle of poverty.

q: What are the key recommendations for future social marketing and social mobilization programs?
a: Future social marketing and social mobilization programs can be sealed and ensured if they offer both short-term and long-term benefits that entice parents to be active influencers for their children to finish schooling. Programs can continue to serve as communication platforms that drive behavioral change as long as the perceived benefits are rationalized by parents.

q: Under what conditions can social marketing programs continue to drive sustained behavioral change?
a: Programs can continue to serve as effective communication platforms as long as the perceived benefits are rationalized by the target audience. Specifically, the perceived benefits must exceed the perceived costs of the action.

q: Who is the primary target audience for the communication strategies discussed in the Eduk-Aksyon Program?
a: The target audience for these communication platforms is the parents. The goal is to influence them to ensure their children finish their schooling.

q: What is the definition of sustainable behavioral change according to the research context?
a: Sustainable behavioral change is described as a by-product of communication through action. This occurs when people realize the perceived benefits and values of making a change in their behavior.

q: In what way does the Eduk-Aksyon Program function as a communication platform?
a: The Eduk-Aksyon Program functions as a communication platform by driving behavioral change in parents through communication-through-action. This occurs via channels such as the distribution of school supplies and the provision of rewards and incentives systems.

q: How does the research link parental behavior to the educational success of children?
a: The research indicates that sustained behavioral change in parents, such as continuing to send children to school, is driven by an interplay of personal motivations and external factors. These include the realization of perceived benefits from schooling, the fulfillment of moral obligations, and the influence of programs that provide rewards, incentives, and school supplies.

q: What role does holistic development play in the context of the Eduk-Aksyon Program?
a: The program initiates holistic development in both mental and spiritual aspects. Parents valued this aspect as an intrinsic factor that contributed to the sustained behavioral change regarding their children's schooling.

q: What is the central purpose of Winnie Aurea D. Corcuera’s investigation into the Haribon Foundation?
a: The investigation aims to understand how the Haribon Foundation uses social media as a communication platform for environmentalism. It specifically explores the mechanisms used to establish an online presence and how environmental communication is sustained in digital advocacy.

q: What are the main findings regarding the role of communication officers in Haribon's digital advocacy?
a: Communication officers serve as crucial vehicles of information between Haribon and its audience. They are advantaged if they are knowledgeable about the advocacies and equipped with the skills to deliver them through social media.

q: What specific social media strategies does the Haribon Foundation employ to promote its mission?
a: The organization uses informational campaigns through creative posts, shares environmental trivia, and 'rides on popular culture' to increase relevance. They also engage in direct conversation with the audience and use linking and tagging to connect with international partners.

q: What research methodology was used to examine Haribon's online environmental advocacy?

q: How do social orders manifest through communication to marginalize individuals with Down Syndrome?

q: How does communication contribute to the marginalization of a child with Down Syndrome?
a: The medical and educational institutions relegated the child to the margins through the words spoken, in documents, and in practice. This communication served the social order's purpose of keeping the child with Down Syndrome in her place in the margins of society.

q: How was the personal narrative used in this critical autoethnography?

q: How does the mother navigate power within the family, medical, and educational institutions?
a: The mother's communicative performance is defined by the family being at the core of the social order, reclaiming power from the medical institution, and negotiating with the power of the educational institution. These constructs illustrate the complex communicative labor required to navigate institutionalized marginalization.

q: In what ways do medical and educational institutions communicate exclusion?
a: Marginalization is surfaced through the specific words spoken to the family, the language used in official documents, and the practical ways in which these institutions operate. These communicative tools reinforce the boundaries of the social order to push children with Down Syndrome to the margins.

q: How does the research view the role of caregivers in negotiating power?
a: The research reveals that the mother's communicative performance was shaped into three constructs: family at the core of the social order, reclaiming power from the medical institution, and negotiating with the power of the educational institution.

q: What is the central problem investigated in Marie Fayne Patricia R. Alvarado's research?

q: What are the main findings regarding the linguistic factors that contribute to the gap between competence and performance?
a: Significant linguistic contributors include L1 interference, poor L2 input in the participants' households, low language aptitude, and a lack of practice during the Critical Period of Language Acquisition. These factors suggest that foundational development and upbringing play vital roles in linguistic expression.

q: Which non-linguistic factors were found to contribute to the discrepancy in online English teachers?
a: The study found that being instrumentally motivated, using indirect learning strategies, and having limited experience with the Communicative Language Teaching approach contribute to the gap. These elements represent the psychological and methodological drivers of the discrepancy.

q: What specific variables were identified as significant predictors of the discrepancy between competence and performance?
a: The specific variables identified as significant predictors include L1 interference, poor L2 input in households, low language aptitude, lack of practice during the Critical Period of Language Acquisition, being instrumentally motivated, use of indirect learning strategies, and limited experience with the Communicative Language Teaching approach. Additionally, motivation and learning strategies were proven to be predictors of the discrepancy.

q: What is the specific learning profile of second language learners likely to manifest competence and performance discrepancies?
a: The learning profile includes L1 interference, poor L2 input in households, low language aptitude, lack of practice during the Critical Period of Language Acquisition, being instrumentally motivated, use of indirect learning strategies, and limited experience with the Communicative Language Teaching approach. Motivation and Learning Strategies are also predictors of this discrepancy.

q: What are the practical implications of these findings for educational institutions?
a: The findings provide an approximate learning profile of second language learners likely to manifest competence and performance discrepancies. This information makes early intervention possible to rectify this gap.

q: What are the limitations or scope of the factors examined in this research?
a: The research focuses on a specific set of linguistic variables including interlanguage, L2 input, language aptitude, and age, alongside non-linguistic factors like attitude and education culture. The study is situated specifically within the context of Filipino online English teachers.

q: How can the findings regarding the Communicative Language Teaching approach impact teacher training?
a: The research suggests that limited experience with the Communicative Language Teaching approach contributes to the discrepancy between competence and performance. Therefore, increasing exposure to communicative approaches can help teachers improve their linguistic performance.

q: What is the primary purpose of Pasana's research regarding BEEd students?
a: The research aims to examine the effects of metacognitive strategy instruction on the metacognitive awareness and reading comprehension performance of BEEd students. It also seeks to determine if a relationship exists between metacognitive awareness and reading comprehension.

q: What were the main findings regarding the impact of metacognitive strategy instruction?
a: Explicit instruction of metacognitive reading strategies led to improvements in both reading comprehension performance and metacognitive awareness. Additionally, a moderate positive relationship was demonstrated between metacognitive awareness and reading comprehension.

q: What specific metacognitive reading strategies were taught to the participants?
a: The instruction focused on teaching planning, monitoring, and evaluating strategies. These strategies were taught to 45 students over a five-week period.

q: What instructional model was used to deliver the metacognitive training?
a: The researcher used the Gradual Release of Responsibility model of instruction to deliver the five-week intervention.

q: What statistical methods were employed to analyze the data?
a: The researcher used T-tests for paired samples to compare pre-test and post-test scores and Spearman’s rho to test the relationship between variables. A frequency test was also conducted to identify which specific strategies were learned most effectively.

q: Who is the target population for this research?
a: The study focused on 45 Bachelor of Elementary Education (BEEd) students. These university-level students were chosen because many struggle to read analytically or adjust their reading to different materials.

q: What are the implications of these findings for higher education curricula?
a: The results have implications for reading instruction at the tertiary level, teacher education, and future research. Students can overcome reading difficulties when they receive appropriate training on reading strategies and are introduced to the concept of metacognition.

q: What is the significance of the relationship between metacognitive awareness and reading comprehension?
a: The study demonstrated a moderate positive relationship between these two variables. This suggests that as metacognitive awareness increases, reading comprehension performance also tends to improve.

q: What instructional model was proven effective for teaching metacognitive strategies?
a: The Gradual Release of Responsibility model was used to teach planning, monitoring, and evaluating strategies over five weeks. This approach successfully led to improvements in students' metacognitive awareness and reading comprehension.

q: What recommendation is made for textbook writers?

q: What is the relationship between teachers' readiness and their attitude toward new literacy?

q: How is new literacy defined in the context of this research?

q: What is the central purpose of Mason H. Williams' investigation into audiobook sequencing?
a: The investigation aims to determine how Reading Before Listening (RBL) and Listening Before Reading (LBR) sequencing methods affect reading comprehension, spelling accuracy, and motivation among Korean university EFL students. It also explores whether alternating between these two methods provides unique cognitive benefits.

q: What are the primary findings regarding the Reading Before Listening (RBL) method?
a: The RBL sequence was found to support stronger spelling accuracy and reading comprehension. Students who switched from LBR to RBL specifically demonstrated improved spelling accuracy.

q: What research methodology did Mason H. Williams employ to collect data?
a: The researcher used an exploratory small case study design involving a longitudinal approach with three participants. Data collection included formative assessments, pre- and post-surveys, reading logs, group discussions, and guided interviews.

q: What are the key conclusions regarding the use of multimodal input?
a: The results suggest that multimodal input provides significant cognitive benefits and support theories such as Cognitive Load, Dual Coding, and Transfer Stage theory. The sequence of audio and text can be strategically manipulated to target specific linguistic skills.

q: What practical recommendations are offered to educators for integrating audiobooks?
a: Educators are suggested to use flexible sequencing tailored to learner needs to enhance comprehension and spelling outcomes. This approach can be used to integrate audiobooks into reading programs.

q: What are the implications of switching between RBL and LBR sequencing?
a: Switching sequences yielded positive results for both groups of students. Transitioning from RBL to LBR enhanced comprehension, while transitioning from LBR to RBL improved spelling accuracy.

q: What directions does the researcher suggest for future research in this area?
a: Future research should involve larger samples, varied text types, and classroom-based implementations to build on these initial insights.

q: How can teachers use audiobook sequencing to target specific linguistic skills?
a: RBL sequencing supports stronger spelling accuracy and comprehension, while LBR sequencing helps students grasp broader meaning and develop listening strategies. Teachers can use flexible sequencing tailored to learner needs to enhance both comprehension and spelling outcomes.

q: What is the central purpose of the sustained community-based in-service training (SCBINSET) program?

q: What were the main findings regarding the content knowledge of the chemistry teachers?

q: How did the training affect the pedagogical competency of the teachers?

q: What methodology was used to assess the impact of the training on teaching competency?

q: What were the key conclusions regarding the durability of the training effects?

q: What specific chemistry topics were covered during the seminar-workshops?

q: What impact did the training have on student learning outcomes?

q: Which specific instruments were utilized to collect data for the research?

q: What are the main findings regarding the quality of mathematical proofs produced by students?

q: What methodology was used to evaluate the quality of the mathematical proofs?
